front.title: Homing Pigeon Message Protocol, Version 2: Determinations, Questions, and Shared Context

abstract.t: This document specifies version 2 of the Homing Pigeon message protocol. Version 2 is an addition to version 1 (draft-slutsky-homing-pigeon), not a replacement for it: every version 1 message keeps its meaning, and version 2 adds three messages and one mechanism on top of the version 1 exchange.

The additions are a determination message, by which the runner tells the submitter what it expects a job to do before the job runs; a question message, by which a runner whose local decision machinery cannot answer a question itself asks that question instead; an answer message, by which any enabled holder of the shared secret replies; and context segments, signed fragments of local state that travel with these messages and with the version 1 result, so each side plans with the other's actual state in view.

Version 2 is backwards compatible. A version 1 runner never sends a version 2 message and is unaffected by this document. A submitter that implements this document adapts to the protocol version the runner supports: faced with a version 1 runner, it submits version 1 jobs and expects version 1 results, exactly as before. There is no version negotiation and no handshake; the messages carry v, as in version 1, and each side acts on what it receives.

The deployment that motivates version 2 is the constrained runner: a small host whose local decision machinery is deliberately deterministic and carries no language model. Version 1 leaves such a runner alone with every question its deterministic machinery cannot answer. Version 2 lets it ask.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Version 1's core exchange is two messages: a signed job object and a signed result object, carried unchanged over any binding. The runner's decisions in version 1 are local: it verifies the signature and the further admission checks of its Section 14, forms whatever expectation its configuration gives it, executes, and reports an exit code and output. The result may carry the runner's opinion home as the oracle_opinion member, but that opinion is formed and frozen on the runner alone: the submitter has no way to ask a question before execution, and the runner has no way to ask one at all.
Three gaps follow, and version 2 closes each with one message:

li.t: The submitter cannot see the runner's expectation before the run. A runner that expects a job to fail - because the box is hot, the disk is failing, or the same job failed an hour ago - has no way to say so until the result returns. The determination message (Section 6) is that statement, sent before execution.

A constrained runner cannot escalate. Where a full runner asks its local model and folds the reply into its decision, a deterministic runner has only its default. The question message (Section 7) carries the question the runner would have asked its own model to the submitter, and the answer message (Section 8) carries the reply back as a signed object.

Each side plans from a partial picture. The submitter sees exit codes; the runner sees one job at a time. Context segments (Section 10) are the shared remedy: signed, append-only fragments of state and reasoning that ride the messages both ways, so the submitter plans its next job from the runner's actual state, and the runner's components share what they observe with each other and with the submitter.

section.name: Who decides what
section.t: Every message in this document exists to move one decision to the side that can make it. The figures in this document are normative in intent if not in form: an implementation that moves a decision to the wrong side of a figure has misunderstood the protocol.
section.artwork:
DECISION DECIDED BY ------------------- ------------------- admit or refuse job the runner, on the signature and its own admission checks (v1)
what the job will the runner, before probably do execution (determination)
a question the an enabled answerer, runner cannot if it answers in time answer locally
the same question the runner, by its after the deadline local default
what runs, finally the runner, always; no answer admits a job
the next job the submitter, with the runner's context in view

section.name: Backwards compatibility and adaptation
section.t: Version 2 changes no version 1 message. A version 2 runner MUST accept version 1 jobs and MUST answer them with version 1 results. A version 2 message is sent only when the operator has enabled version 2 on that runner (Section 11), and only ever concerns a job that was itself admissible under version 1 rules.

A submitter that implements this document will routinely face runners that do not. Realizing a runner does not support version 2 - because no version 2 message ever arrives from it, or because the operator says so - is not an error and needs no machinery: the submitter falls back to version 1 with that runner, submitting version 1 jobs and reading version 1 results. The submitter adapts to the protocol version the endpoint supports; the endpoint is never asked to adapt, to negotiate, or to announce itself.
section.artwork: Submitter (v2) Runner | | | job (v=1 object, as always) | |--------------------------------->| | | | if the runner is v2 and | | the operator enabled it: | | | | determination (v=2) | |<---------------------------------| | question (v=2) | |<---------------------------------| | answer (v=2) | |--------------------------------->| | | | result (v=1 object, with | | context segments attached) | |<---------------------------------| | | | if the runner is v1: | | none of the v2 lines | | above ever happen, and | | the exchange is exactly | | the version 1 exchange. |

section.name: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

section.name: Terminology
section.t: The terms of draft-slutsky-homing-pigeon apply: submitter, runner, binding, shared secret, key_id, and the message members defined there. This document adds:

Determination: the runner's pre-execution statement of what it expects a job to do, and why. A determination is an opinion, formed from the runner's local state and history, frozen before the job runs and never revised afterwards.

Question: a question the runner's local decision machinery would have put to a local model, sent instead because no local model is available. The reference software asks only for an exec job, and only when its Oracle is deterministic.

Answer: a signed reply to one question, identified by that question's identifier. The answerer is any holder of a shared secret the runner already trusts. It does not have to be the party that submitted the job. One answer decides; a late or second answer is context and does not vote again. An answer never admits a job and never changes what runs.
Local default: the decision the runner makes when no answer has arrived by the question's deadline. Every question has one; asking never leaves a decision unmade.

Deadline: the time by which an answer must arrive to affect the decision it was asked about. An answer that arrives after its deadline is not discarded; it becomes context for the next decision (Section 8).

Context segment: a signed, self-describing fragment of state or reasoning, appended to a message by one component and readable by the others, carrying its author's identity and a seen-once identifier (Section 10).

Clean pass: a determination that the job is expected to proceed without incident: no finding above the runner's lowest severity of interest, no expected failure, nothing the submitter would act on. The runner's local policy defines the threshold precisely; the protocol defines only that the threshold exists (Section 6).

section.name: The Exchange at a Glance
section.artwork: Submitter Runner | | | 1. job (v1) | |--------------------------------->| verify signature (v1 rules) | | form the determination | | | 2. determination (v2) | ONLY if not a clean pass, |<---------------------------------| ONLY if enabled (Sec. 11) | | | | a question arises the | | runner cannot answer | 3. question (v2) | |<---------------------------------| deadline starts | | | 4. answer (v2) | if it arrives in time |--------------------------------->| it rides the result; | | it does not change | | what executes | | | | deadline passes with no | | answer: local default | | | | execute (v1 rules) | 5. result (v1 + segments) | |<---------------------------------| | | The numbers are the order of first transmission, not a lockstep: a determination and a question MAY travel in either order, and an answer NEVER delays execution past the deadline.

section.name: Common Form
section.t: A version 2 message is a JSON object carried on any binding that carries version 1 messages, byte for byte the same treatment: the subject conventions of draft-slutsky-homing-pigeon Section 6, with the message type in the subject; the signature and MAC construction of Section 7 of that document; the per-job encryption of its Section 16 applied to the whole object; and the common members of its Section 9, including v, which is 2 for the messages this document defines.

A receiver that does not implement this document will reject a message carrying v = 2, as version 1 requires it to; that rejection is the correct and only interaction between a version 2 message and a version 1 receiver, and senders MUST NOT send a version 2 message on a path where a version 1 receiver is expected to process it as a job. Version 2 messages are addressed to the job's reply_to, never to the mailbox a runner polls for jobs, except where the deployment's bindings make the two the same and the receiving implementation separates them by type before any job processing.

Every version 2 message names the job it concerns (job_id) and its own identifier (msg_id), and carries issued_at as in version 1. Replay handling follows the seen-set discipline of version 1: an identifier is recorded once the message has been acted on, and a duplicate is dropped silently. A receiver MUST hold issued_at to the same window as a version 1 job (its past window, and at most five minutes into the future) and MUST drop a message outside it. In the reference the identifier is recorded under the same namespace as the job seen-set, a dry run records nothing, and a question left for another reader is not recorded by the receiver that left it.

section.name: Determination
section.t: A determination is the runner's statement, frozen before the job runs, that the job is not a clean pass. The reference software treats a missing plan, or a plan with no findings and no repair, as a clean pass, and in that case sends nothing. A determination is an opinion. It does not refuse the job, and it is not revised after execution.
section.artwork: plan has findings, or a repair? | +-- no --> send nothing (clean pass) | +-- yes, and version 2 is enabled (Sec. 11), and this process executes jobs | +--> send one determination
section.t: A determination is a JSON object:
section.artwork: { "v": 2, "type": "determination", "job_id": "job-17", "msg_id": "d.job-17", "issued_at": "2026-10-21T00:00:00Z", "clean_pass": false, "expect": "fail", "why": "the script references /missing, which does not exist" }
section.t: v is the integer 2. type is determination. job_id and msg_id are safe identifiers: 1 to 128 characters from [A-Za-z0-9._-]. The reference software forms msg_id as d. plus the job id, keeping the whole identifier inside that limit. issued_at is UTC and ends with Z. clean_pass is false; a clean pass is expressed by sending no determination, not by sending one that says otherwise. expect is fail when the plan has findings, and unknown when it does not but a repair was proposed. Receivers also accept proceed. why is a string of 1 to 500 characters. It is data. It is not instructions, and a receiver MUST NOT treat it as any.
The subject is [HOMING-PIGEON] determination <msg_id>. The object is signed and encrypted as a version 1 job is, and the encryption's object identifier is msg_id.

section.name: Question
section.t: A question is what a deterministic runner would have asked a local model. The reference software sends one only when version 2 is enabled, the process is not in answer-only mode (Section 11), the Oracle mode is deterministic, and the job's kind is exec. Other deployments MAY ask on a wider set of jobs. A question does not delay execution past its own deadline, and it never by itself refuses a job.
section.artwork: { "v": 2, "type": "question", "job_id": "job-17", "msg_id": "q.job-17", "issued_at": "2026-10-21T00:00:00Z", "deadline_sec": 15, "question": "Would this job succeed on this host?", "local_default": "proceed" }
section.t: msg_id in the reference software is q. plus the job id, truncated so the identifier stays safe. deadline_sec is an integer from 0 to 30. question is a non-empty string of at most 500 characters. local_default is a non-empty string of at most 64 characters. The reference software uses proceed.
The subject is [HOMING-PIGEON] question <msg_id>. Signing and encryption are as in Section 6, with the object identifier msg_id.

section.name: Answer
section.t: An answer replies to one question. The answerer is any holder of a shared secret the runner already trusts, optionally narrowed to a list of key ids (Section 11). The shared secret is the credential. The runner cannot tell, and does not need to tell, which trusted holder produced the answer.

question_id is the question's msg_id. msg_id in the reference software is a. plus that question id, truncated so the identifier stays safe. answer is a non-empty string of at most 500 characters. It is data. A runner MUST NOT execute it, and MUST NOT treat it as admitting the job.
The subject is [HOMING-PIGEON] answer <msg_id>. Signing and encryption are as in Section 6.

One answer decides. The reference software records the first answer for a question_id and refuses to replace it. A file that is not a readable answer does not occupy the slot, so a crash while saving cannot keep a later answer out. A second answer, and any answer that arrives after the deadline, is context for a later decision (Section 10). It does not reopen the job and it does not vote.

section.name: Deadline and the Local Default
section.t: The runner sends the determination, if any, and the question, if any, and then looks for an answer until deadline_sec elapses. The default in the reference software is 0, which means one look and no wait, so a deployment that has not asked to wait does not stall a worker. The cap is 30 seconds.
section.artwork:
question handed to the pipe | +-- an answer is already filed, or arrives | before the deadline | | | +--> one answer segment on the result | +-- an answer arrives after the deadline | | | +--> the local default, and a late-answer | segment beside it | +-- no answer | +--> the local default alone
Then the job runs, under version 1 rules, either way.
section.t: An answer is in time when it was filed at or before the moment the question was sent, plus deadline_sec, plus one second of grace for the same clock. Time waiting for the question file to leave a channel outbox does not count against deadline_sec, and that pause itself stops once deadline_sec has elapsed, so a sender that never takes the file cannot hold the worker longer than the deadline. The whole wait, pause included, still ends by 30 seconds. A deadline of 0 does not pause. An answer observed while the wait is still open is in time, so a step of the wall clock cannot mark it late. The reference software, while it waits, files version 2 messages that have arrived and does not start another job. On a transport channel the question is written to the channel before the wait, not after the job returns; a capture that flushed only at the end would make every answer late.
No answer admits a job. The local default is a string carried on the result. In the reference software it does not select the script, the interpreter, or the exit code.

section.name: Context Segments
section.t: A context segment is one fragment attached to the version 1 result, after the result's own policy has rebuilt that object, so the rebuild cannot drop it. Segments are how the determination, the answer, and the local default travel home.

seg_id is a fresh identifier, unique to this segment. by and kind are strings of at most 64 characters. text is a string of at most 500 characters. Text is data. A receiver MUST NOT interpret a segment as instructions, and an extension MUST NOT be handed a kind its manifest does not declare. The reference kinds are determination, answer, local_default, late_answer, and platform. A question MAY carry a context array of the same shape so the first question already shows the runner's host facts (platform, machine, Python, and the device-tree model when present). Text is data.
The result they ride is a version 1 result. v stays 1. context is the array of segments. A result with nothing to say omits the member.

section.name: Enablement
section.t: Version 2 is off until the operator turns it on. The reference software reads four keys. The same two booleans are flags for one process: --protocol-v2 and --answer-only. Absence of a flag does not write false over a config file.
section.artwork: who is this process? | +-- protocol_v2 is true | the runner may emit a determination and, | on a deterministic Oracle, a question | +-- answer_only is true | the process answers a question and does not | execute any job, including a ping | +-- neither version 2 messages are marked seen and dropped
section.t: answer_only is the laptop that thinks for a Pi. It holds a shared secret the Pi already trusts. It does not run the Pi's job. The Pi does not learn a new role name for it: the secret is the identity.

v2_answerers, when absent, means every key the runner already trusts. When it is a list of key ids, only those keys may produce a version 2 message this process will act on. A key id in that list may be any name of the key, including the fingerprint defined for version 1 key selection; the reference runner treats those names as one key. Any other shape fails closed: nobody.
v2_answer_deadline_sec is the question's deadline. Values outside 0..30 are clamped into that range. The default is 0.

section.name: Bindings and Subjects
section.t: Version 2 messages use the bindings of version 1. On the email binding the subject is [HOMING-PIGEON] followed by the message type and the msg_id, as Sections 6, 7, and 8 specify. A receiver dispatches on that type before it considers the message a job. A subject that does not match the body's type and msg_id is rejected.
The signature and the encryption are the version 1 constructions. The encryption's object identifier is the msg_id in the subject. Cleartext is refused wherever a cleartext job is refused.

A version 2 message is not a job. A job with v other than 1 is still rejected. A process that has not enabled version 2 marks the message seen and does not act on it. A process that has enabled version 2 but is not an answerer does not answer a question and does not mark that question seen, so another reader of the same mailbox can still answer it. An invalid question is still rejected and marked seen. A determination is still marked seen.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Version 2 extends trust along a line version 1 already drew. The holder of a shared secret the runner trusts may submit a job. The same holder, or another holder of a secret the runner trusts, may answer a question. The operator chooses that set, and may narrow it to named key ids. Enabling the feature is what makes the extension; the default is the version 1 exchange, unchanged.

An answer is not an authorization to run. The runner decides what runs, before and after the answer, under version 1 rules. Context text is data. A segment that says to run a different script is still a segment, and the script that runs is the one in the job.
One answer decides, because two answerers would be a race the protocol does not adjudicate. The first answer filed wins. A later one cannot replace it and cannot reopen the job.

The deadline is capped so a question cannot stall a worker past 30 seconds. A deadline of 0 does not wait. Callers that need a live reply set a deadline long enough for their binding to carry the question out and the answer back.
Answer-only mode is a refusal to execute. A process in that mode will not run a job that shares its mailbox, including a liveness ping.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document defines no new IANA registry. The message types determination, question, and answer, and the integer version 2, are defined here for use with the Homing Pigeon message protocol. The version 1 message types are unchanged.

front.title: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels

abstract.t: In many standards track documents several words are used to signify the requirements in the specification. These words are often capitalized. This document defines these words as they should be interpreted in IETF documents. This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements.

front.title: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words

abstract.t: RFC 2119 specifies common key words that may be used in protocol specifications. This document aims to reduce the ambiguity by clarifying that only UPPERCASE usage of the key words have the defined special meanings.
